« Martin, Sébastien » <smartin@universite-paris.fr> le 26/12/2023 10:59:38
À : « vincent.leblanc@lumieresante.fr » <vincent.leblanc@lumieresante.fr>
Cc : « christine.dupont@lumieresante.fr » <christine.dupont@lumieresante.fr>
Objet : RE : Visite à Lyon

Cher Vincent / Christine,

Merci d’être venus à Paris pour présenter un aperçu des projets. Nous avons apprécié cette rencontre avec vous et vos collègues et sommes impatients de collaborer avec Lumière Santé. Je tiens également à transmettre les remerciements de mon équipe pour le dîner.

Nous souhaitons vous donner une mise à jour sur notre projet et obtenir des retours ainsi que des informations complémentaires avant notre prochaine visite à Lyon, le 19 janvier. Notre projet s’orientera vers la troisième option que vous avez mentionnée. Nous envisageons d’aborder une partie des services aux patients ambulatoires. Nous étudions deux pistes concernant ce sujet et aimerions approfondir soit (i) la manière dont les patients sont accueillis et recommander de nouveaux processus pour améliorer leur prise en charge, soit (ii) l’analyse de la chaîne de services et proposer des recommandations pour de futurs investissements.

Cependant, nous aimerions obtenir davantage d’informations sur les services ambulatoires avant de définir précisément l’étendue du projet. Nous sommes aussi très ouverts à vos suggestions, surtout si vous aviez en tête un périmètre plus large ou différent ; n’hésitez pas à nous en faire part.

Nous n’avons pas encore étudié en détail les documents introductifs reçus la semaine dernière, mais voici quelques questions spécifiques aux services ambulatoires :

- Pouvons-nous consulter le plan d’affaires global ou un résumé plus détaillé que celui figurant dans le rapport annuel ?
- Quelle est la philosophie tarifaire et la structure générale ?
- Qui sont les patients et comment sont-ils accueillis ?
- Que feraient ces patients s’ils ne bénéficiaient pas des services de Lumière Santé ?
- Quels sont les projets et capacités d’expansion internationale ?
- Existe-t-il un résumé des aspects réglementaires importants que nous pourrions avoir ?

Si ces informations ne figurent pas dans les documents reçus, pourriez-vous nous orienter vers d’autres sources ?

Après examen des documents, nous souhaiterions organiser un appel téléphonique avec vous et/ou un collègue impliqué directement dans les services ambulatoires. Je vous contacterai début janvier pour en discuter davantage. En attendant, n’hésitez pas à me joindre au 01 45 67 89 10 si besoin.

Cordialement,
L’Équipe Tiger Services Ambulatoires
Raphaël
Denis
Jacques
Omar
Stéphane
Claude

Subject: Highlander vs. Outback, per Autotrend.com
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Tasman Ridge Resources Ltd notes that the Highlander was introduced several years ago as a premium alternative to the popular Outback sport-utility vehicle. The challenge was that the Outback could match the Highlander’s luxury features and, in some instances, came with a higher price tag. For the 2024 model year, Highlander has been further differentiated from the Outback. The result is a well-rounded SUV offering enhanced handling and a generous array of features.

This near-luxury SUV is available with either a 3.8-liter V6 engine producing 215 horsepower or a 4.5-liter V8 delivering 245 horsepower. Both powertrains are paired with a smooth six-speed automatic transmission. The new V8 provides ample and refined power, although fuel efficiency remains average.

The Highlander has been redesigned inside and out, with results that are very appealing. Its front fascia is now clearly distinct from the Outback, featuring a brushed-metal grille and striking LED headlamps. Inside, satin-aluminum trim embellishments create a sophisticated, high-tech ambiance, moving away from its previous look as an Outback variant.

Mechanical improvements go well beyond aesthetics. A brand-new independent rear suspension with a unique frame design allows the rear floor to drop by 180 millimeters, accommodating a third-row seat while increasing ground clearance to 235 millimeters. Ride comfort and handling have also been substantially enhanced. The Highlander now feels more composed on the road with flatter cornering dynamics. A 65-millimeter wider track further improves stability and interior spaciousness.

Noise, vibration, and harshness (NVH) have been significantly reduced. There is a 50% reduction in cabin air infiltration, complemented by a refined transmission for a quieter driving experience, although some vibration from the all-wheel-drive system can still be felt through the floor.

New convenience features include a standard six-way power driver's seat, with options for adjustable pedals, heated front seats, and heated side mirrors. Safety enhancements feature optional side curtain airbags, a reinforced body structure, and a lower front bumper to improve crash compatibility. Later in the model year, rollover sensors and an advanced traction and stability control system will be introduced.

The Highlander’s strengths rest in its comprehensive features, powerful engine lineup, and upgraded rear suspension. While there are many SUVs available, if you desire an Outback but prefer something more refined and capable, the Highlander is well worth considering.

Assunto: Caminhada pela Cura do Diabetes Juvenil!

Mal posso acreditar que mais um ano já passou! No domingo, dia 28 de outubro, acontecerá a Caminhada pela Cura do Diabetes Juvenil! Novamente este ano, estou convocando participantes para a minha equipe ou simplesmente pedindo o seu apoio. Sei que vocês já recebem muitos pedidos de ajuda, mas vou pedir mesmo assim — a maioria de vocês me conhece bem!

Sendo eu mesma portadora de diabetes insulinodependente, sinto que é minha obrigação apoiar todos os esforços para encontrar uma cura para essa doença que afeta tantas crianças e adultos! Muitos de vocês acompanham meu dia a dia lidando com essa condição, especialmente a cada refeição, quando preciso aplicar a insulina e checar a glicemia várias vezes ao dia. Diagnostiquei a doença há apenas quatro anos, mas a sua contribuição faz toda a diferença. Espera-se que em até dois anos seja liberada uma insulina inalável, que eliminará a necessidade das injeções dolorosas.

Sei que vocês têm sido muito solicitados por diversas instituições este ano, mas espero que considerem apoiar a Fundação Brasileira do Diabetes (FBD), assim como eu faço. Por favor, pensem em se juntar à minha equipe ou a uma das várias equipes da BrasiLog Transportes e ajudem a encontrar uma cura para o diabetes! Cada participante ou patrocinador que contribuir com R$ 25,00 ou mais receberá uma camiseta oficial da BrasiLog para o evento! Se R$ 25,00 não estiver no seu orçamento, você pode comprar um "Tênis FBD" por apenas R$ 5,00, que será exposto no refeitório da empresa no dia 26 de outubro. Como sempre, a BrasiLog Transportes irá igualar todas as doações!

Muito obrigada pelo seu apoio e espero encontrar todos vocês no dia 28!

Ana Silva

-----Original Message-----
From: Sanjay Kulkarni
Sent: Thursday, 24 May 2021 08:48 AM
To: Anil Desai; Ramesh Patel; Kavita Singh; Ravi Sharma; Neha Joshi; Arjun Mehta
Cc: Meera Kapoor; Neha Joshi; Rajesh Nair; Swati Mehta; Priya Nair
Subject: Mumbai Market Update

The Mumbai Electricity Distribution Company’s filing confirms that the ABX143 tariff freeze at 6.5 INR/kWh does not cover Direct Access customers.

In hearings concerning the Distribution Company’s proposed tariff increase for large consumers:

- The company has proposed allocating all retained generation capacity to small consumers (below 100 kW). Large consumers would be served by the state authority or through Direct Access. Multiple stakeholders have expressed significant concerns about this.

- It is notable that the company’s calculated tariff increase under their proposal is 2.86 INR/kWh. If large consumers are allocated a portion of retained generation, the increase rises slightly to 2.99 INR/kWh. In that scenario, large consumers retain a CTC (related to power purchase agreements and other long-term stranded costs) that they would otherwise lose.

Our aim is to secure an order that: 1) excludes Direct Access customers from any tariff increase (the proposed 2.86 INR/kWh); 2) excludes Direct Access from any surcharge related to under-recovery during the tariff freeze (amount currently unknown); 3) prorates the surcharge related to under-recovery if the customer switches from Direct Access to bundled service during the freeze period; and 4) ensures a return to market pricing once the freeze ends.

The regulatory commission’s decisions on these matters are expected by 28 June. There is no discussion restricting movement between bundled service and Direct Access. Regarding our priorities, points 1, 2, and 4 have a strong likelihood of success; point 3 is about 50/50.

From: Ellis, Fiona
Sent: Thursday, 8 November 2023 19:25
To: James, James; Clarke, Emma
Subject: Corporate Secretary Replacement

As you both likely know, I will officially retire on 1 January 2024; therefore, the meeting on 12 November will be my last and an ideal opportunity to appoint my successor. Thank you for allowing me to continue serving as your corporate secretary after stepping down from my role at Halcyon Mutual Bank. I don’t think I could have let go abruptly, and I have greatly enjoyed this position because of my respect for the directors and most of the senior management. (I’ll reserve commentary on a few former members of management who are no longer with us.)

Since James became involved, I have really appreciated the positive impact on morale and operational results—it’s been clear to see. I have also been a long-time admirer of Emma and have truly enjoyed collaborating with Robert Harris. Therefore, it is my sincere hope and recommendation that Robert be chosen to succeed me. He has consistently demonstrated capability in this role—in fact, he has been performing many of the duties for quite some time, except for the actual minute-taking, which he has kindly relieved me of on several occasions. Robert is a person of integrity, loyalty, and dedication, and I know the Directors think highly of him. I hope you both agree.

I will miss you both, and Emma, I would love to meet for lunch with you and Robert sometime. I am also happy to provide any support or advice I can offer.

Thank you once again.

With warm regards,
Fiona Ellis

Subject: Cutoff Time for End-of-Day Gas Transactions
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Dear all,

A couple of weeks ago, I spoke with each of you regarding this matter, but it was postponed due to other urgent priorities. Nevertheless, you all agreed that establishing a standard cutoff time for UK gas, power, and liquids transactions would be appropriate.

The optimal approach would be to set the cutoff at 4pm daily. To provide some context, I reviewed yesterday’s activity to see how many deals were executed after 4pm London time. There were three UK Gas trades and two European Gas trades. Post-4pm, any unsettled deals would automatically roll over to the next business day. However, for deals that do not roll over after 4pm, the respective risk teams will need to treat them as the following day’s transactions. I’m unsure how this might impact Risk’s procedures for traders’ position reporting, since official books would exclude these late trades. Would Risk be able to produce supplemental reports each morning to ensure desks have accurate positions?

Please share any feedback you may have, and in any case, kindly confirm whether a 4pm cutoff works for your teams.

Best regards,
Alex
Meridian Law & Advisory LLP
x48219

James – are there any potential issues with the daily position reconciliation?
Claire – we touched on this briefly a few weeks ago; any additional thoughts?
subject: Cutoff Time for End-of-Day Gas Transactions
body:
Dear all,

A couple of weeks ago, I spoke with each of you regarding this matter, but it was postponed due to other urgent priorities. Nevertheless, you all agreed that establishing a standard cutoff time for UK gas, power, and liquids transactions would be appropriate.

The optimal approach would be to set the cutoff at 4pm daily. To provide some context, I reviewed yesterday’s activity to see how many deals were executed after 4pm London time. There were three UK Gas trades and two European Gas trades. Post-4pm, any unsettled deals would automatically roll over to the next business day. However, for deals that do not roll over after 4pm, the respective risk teams will need to treat them as the following day’s transactions. I’m unsure how this might impact Risk’s procedures for traders’ position reporting, since official books would exclude these late trades. Would Risk be able to produce supplemental reports each morning to ensure desks have accurate positions?

Please share any feedback you may have, and in any case, kindly confirm whether a 4pm cutoff works for your teams.

Best regards,
Alex
Meridian Law & Advisory LLP
x48219

James – are there any potential issues with the daily position reconciliation?
Claire – we touched on this briefly a few weeks ago; any additional thoughts?

Cc: Marthe Delorme <marthe.delorme@lumieresante.fr>
Subject: Invitation to Participate in the Lumière Santé Regional Healthcare Innovation Workshop
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Dear Dr. Martin,

Please find below a formal invitation to attend, participate, and present at the Lumière Santé Regional Healthcare Innovation Workshop. A printed copy of this invitation will follow shortly.

Dr. Martin
Lumière Santé SAS
12 Rue de la Santé
75014 Paris, France

Paris, March 12, 2024

I am pleased to invite you to join us as a speaker at the upcoming Lumière Santé Regional Healthcare Innovation Workshop. Each invited presentation will be allocated thirty minutes, followed by approximately ten minutes for discussion. This workshop, supported by a grant from the French Ministry of Health, will differ from typical industry conferences by focusing on the practical applications of healthcare technologies and innovations currently driving progress within hospital groups and medical laboratories. Moreover, the event will highlight the collaborative efforts bridging healthcare providers, research institutions, and governmental bodies.

The workshop will be held at the Hôtel de la Santé in Lyon on April 27-28. We are able to cover travel expenses, accommodation, and meals for all invited speakers, and can assist with travel arrangements if needed.

We sincerely hope you will accept this invitation. Should you agree, please send us your presentation title, a brief abstract, and any technical requirements for your talk.

We look forward to welcoming you to Lyon.

Kind regards,

Sophie Durand
Lumière Santé SAS
subject: Invitation to Participate in the Lumière Santé Regional Healthcare Innovation Workshop
body:
Dear Dr. Martin,

Please find below a formal invitation to attend, participate, and present at the Lumière Santé Regional Healthcare Innovation Workshop. A printed copy of this invitation will follow shortly.

Dr. Martin
Lumière Santé SAS
12 Rue de la Santé
75014 Paris, France

Paris, March 12, 2024

I am pleased to invite you to join us as a speaker at the upcoming Lumière Santé Regional Healthcare Innovation Workshop. Each invited presentation will be allocated thirty minutes, followed by approximately ten minutes for discussion. This workshop, supported by a grant from the French Ministry of Health, will differ from typical industry conferences by focusing on the practical applications of healthcare technologies and innovations currently driving progress within hospital groups and medical laboratories. Moreover, the event will highlight the collaborative efforts bridging healthcare providers, research institutions, and governmental bodies.

The workshop will be held at the Hôtel de la Santé in Lyon on April 27-28. We are able to cover travel expenses, accommodation, and meals for all invited speakers, and can assist with travel arrangements if needed.

We sincerely hope you will accept this invitation. Should you agree, please send us your presentation title, a brief abstract, and any technical requirements for your talk.

We look forward to welcoming you to Lyon.

Kind regards,

Sophie Durand
Lumière Santé SAS

headers.Subject: Invitation to Participate in the Lumière Santé Regional Healthcare Innovation Workshop

Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Dear Mark,

If we consider this from a Hamburg index perspective, how would it appear? I believe the client wants to set a floating price based on an index but is looking for some guidance on the appropriate basis relative to Hamburg. This isn’t a firm offer since there’s no actual transaction planned; it’s more of a market indication. It’s a bit unusual, but the more competitive our price is against Hamburg, the better our chances of securing the deal. We should present a strong indicative bid, subject to credit approval and other conditions. When it comes time to finalize, which is unlikely given the units’ lack of historical data, the market price could be quite different.

Best regards,
Michael

Subject: Succession Announcement
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Dear Team,

I am pleased to announce that the Board has approved my recommendation to appoint Michael Lawson as Chief Executive Officer, effective following our next board meeting on March 15, 2024. Michael will continue to serve as Managing Director and Chief Operating Officer. I will remain as Chairman of the Board and will continue to work closely with Michael on the strategic direction and daily operations of Tasman Ridge Resources Ltd.

Michael will step into this role at a time when the company is performing exceptionally well and positioned for significant growth. He is more than ready to lead, and after 18 years as CEO, I am ready to focus on a new role within the company.

Our succession plan has been thoughtfully developed over time, allowing Michael and me to combine our strengths to build a company that consistently exceeds expectations, including our own. We look forward to deepening our partnership as Michael takes on his expanded responsibilities.

There are no plans for further changes to our leadership team or shifts in our strategic direction at this time.

Please join me in congratulating Michael on his new role. I am confident 2024 will be a successful year for Tasman Ridge Resources Ltd.

Warm regards,
David Harper
Chairman, Tasman Ridge Resources Ltd

-----Original Message-----
From: Thompson, Laura
Sent: Tuesday, 30 April 2002 16:09
To: Harris, James; Bennett, Michael; Clarke, Sarah; Palmer, Emily
Cc: O'Neill, Patrick; Davies, Helen; 'mark.evans@cwt.com'; 'sproctor@akllp.com'; Lewis, Daniel; Foster, Rachel; 'michael.koss@uk.pwcglobal.com'; 'jeffrey.benton@uk.pwcglobal.com'; Morgan, Adam
Subject: Outcome of the TCO Bankruptcy Hearing Related to EES Matters

Here is a brief update on last week’s bankruptcy hearing for Columbia Gas Transmission (TCO) concerning the EES issues:

- TCO agreed to withdraw the part of their motion related to EES. The pipeline confirmed that EES has been utilising their transport contracts and has continued to pay invoices since the bankruptcy petition date.
- The £1.5 million claim that TCO had previously included in the Halcyon "set off amount" (i.e., the outstanding demand charges for EES agreements through to contract expiry) has been removed from TCO’s motion.
- The minimum OBA/pooling agreement monthly balance should no longer be required by the pipeline. (Note: Initially, TCO appeared to be using EES's minimum balance to offset Halcyon & EES obligations.)

Subject: Outcome of the TCO Bankruptcy Hearing Related to EES Matters

Here is a brief update on last week’s bankruptcy hearing for Columbia Gas Transmission (TCO) concerning the EES issues:

Subject: A&M/UT Flag Football Invitation

Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Baring Consulting are pleased to sponsor the 2nd Annual Aggie-Longhorn Flag Football Challenge on Saturday, 18th November. This event aims to raise funds for both universities while celebrating the competitive spirit of the third oldest rivalry in college football. This year marks the 107th encounter between Texas A&M University and The University of Texas, with the Big 12 South Title potentially at stake!

Kestrel and Baring Consulting are sponsoring the event, but we need your support as players and fundraisers. The funds raised will contribute to the general scholarship funds of each university.

Event details:
Date: Saturday, 18th November
Time: 10:00 a.m. – approximately 4:00 p.m. (Warm-up at 9:30 a.m.)
Location: Stratford High School Practice Fields (off Dairy Ashford, south of I-10)
Food and Drinks: Schulze’s BBQ (complimentary, courtesy of Kestrel)
Eligibility: Full-time employees and/or their spouses (Players must have graduated from Texas A&M or The University of Texas)
Team Jerseys: Provided by Kestrel and Baring Consulting
Format: 7 players on the field, with at least 1 female player at all times
Team Size: Recommended 8-10 players per team (maximum 10)
Please contact the team captains to sign up promptly to secure your place.

Prizes:
The winning team will receive 16 tickets to the A&M/UT game in Austin on Friday, 24th November
The winners will also hold the prestigious "Horns Down/Horns Up" trophy until next year!

Fundraising Goal: The committee aims to raise $16,000 for each university, requiring a $2,000 contribution per team, supplemented by corporate matching funds.

Last year’s event featured a dramatic comeback as the Kestrel Aggies Team 1 triumphed over the Kestrel Longhorns Team 1, taking home the tickets and trophy. This year, expect the Longhorns (and Baring Consulting) to be determined to even the score!

Thanks to a generous donation from the UT Alumni, redirected to the A&M Foundation, we have permanently endowed scholarships in memory of the 12 Aggies who lost their lives in last year’s Bonfire tragedy. We believe this event is a valued tradition for both companies and are proud to support these vital scholarships.

If you wish to participate or get involved, please contact one of the team captains below by close of business on Friday, 3rd November (phone or email). Team selections will be made on a first-come, first-served basis.

Aggies              Longhorns
Mark Stevenson  Ext 33272        Alan Griffiths  Ext 31944
James Harper       Ext 58410        Simon Clarke      Ext 37942

Subject: NAAG Engagement
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Dear Team,

I have finally connected with Anjali Sharma, our contact at the National Association of State Advocates ("NASA") regarding their role on telecom matters, particularly concerning Section 271 approvals.

Anjali informed me that there is no formal group effort in place (i.e., no telecom committee or a designated advocate leading telecom issues). Individual state advocates may get involved on a case-by-case basis. For instance, the Maharashtra State Advocate, Rajesh Kulkarni, recently opposed Reliance Communications' application for 271 approval, but the regulatory authority still granted Reliance’s petition.

Anjali suggests we leverage the state advocates as much as possible. For example, if we have evidence showing a lack of local competition, we should share this with the relevant state advocate and ask them to represent our interests. Anjali acknowledges that Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd. supports competitive markets, and typically the state advocates would align with our stance — so this is something to keep in mind moving forward. While there is no certainty that the regulator will heed the advocates, it could be a worthwhile approach.

Please share any thoughts or feedback you may have.

Best regards,
Rina Patel
subject: NAAG Engagement
body:
Dear Team,

I have finally connected with Anjali Sharma, our contact at the National Association of State Advocates ("NASA") regarding their role on telecom matters, particularly concerning Section 271 approvals.

Anjali informed me that there is no formal group effort in place (i.e., no telecom committee or a designated advocate leading telecom issues). Individual state advocates may get involved on a case-by-case basis. For instance, the Maharashtra State Advocate, Rajesh Kulkarni, recently opposed Reliance Communications' application for 271 approval, but the regulatory authority still granted Reliance’s petition.

Anjali suggests we leverage the state advocates as much as possible. For example, if we have evidence showing a lack of local competition, we should share this with the relevant state advocate and ask them to represent our interests. Anjali acknowledges that Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd. supports competitive markets, and typically the state advocates would align with our stance — so this is something to keep in mind moving forward. While there is no certainty that the regulator will heed the advocates, it could be a worthwhile approach.

Please share any thoughts or feedback you may have.

Best regards,
Rina Patel

To: Sara Moraes <sara.moraes@brasilog.com.br>
Subject: FW: Summary of Meeting on Storage Allocation Adjustments
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Dear Marina,

Below is the memo I circulated on March 15th summarizing the March 12th meeting. Please refer to the second bullet point in my summary. I recall Ana was unable to attend that day, but Rafael was very engaged throughout the discussion.

I was unable to locate the copy I originally sent, but fortunately, Carlos still had his version.

-----Original Message-----
From: Carlos Mendes
Sent: Tuesday, April 2, 2024 9:45 AM
To: Silva, Mariana
Subject: FW: Summary of Meeting on Storage Allocation Adjustments

For your information.

-----Original Message-----
From: Silva, Mariana
Sent: Friday, March 15, 2024 11:30 AM
To: Costa, Ana; Oliveira, Lucas; Ferreira, Pedro; Mendes, Carlos; Rodrigues, Tiago; Almeida, Sofia; Santos, Bruno; Lima, Eduardo; Moreira, Paula; Gomes, Thiago; Barbosa, Renata; Pinto, Marcelo; Alves, Camila; Souza, Rafael; Carvalho, Daniela
Cc: Pereira, Ricardo; Nunes, Fernanda
Subject: Summary of Meeting on Storage Allocation Adjustments

Please find below a summary of our recent meeting. Should you wish to discuss further, feel free to reach out.

Subdivision of Field Area into Two Regions / Allocation by Zone
It was decided to divide the Field Area storage group into two regions: South of Vale Verde and North of Vale Verde, instead of three regions or allocation by individual points. Should additional subdivisions be necessary in the future, we can implement those changes accordingly. Updates to the CAS system will be required. I have spoken with Ricardo Pereira and Fernanda Nunes, who advised that the updates are straightforward and can be completed within a few days.
Rafael Souza and I will identify which deferred delivery points fall within these new field regions and then provide this information to Ricardo and Fernanda.

Question: Should this change be implemented immediately or postponed until the start of the withdrawal season?

Revision from ‘net zero’ methodology / Ensure minimum activity level
We agreed to postpone this issue for the time being. The scheduled activity driving the allocation process does not necessarily reflect actual pipeline operations. Typically, the flexibility provided by the Vale Verde Field enables Gas Control to adjust operations to maintain the required minimum injection/withdrawal levels for the Redenção and Laguna storage sites. Further analysis is needed. Pedro Ferreira, Bruno Santos, and I will continue to monitor system conditions affecting physical storage to evaluate if any additional adjustments are warranted.

Notification when final scheduled volume exceeds operational capacity
The IT department will update the scheduling procedure to include a step where the final net scheduled storage volume is compared against the operational capacity for storage. Should the final scheduled volume exceed operational capacity, I will receive an email notification. The goal is to track these occurrences and assess the scale of the issue. I will coordinate with Carlos Mendes to finalize this process.

Best regards,
Mariana Silva
BrasiLog Transportes S.A.

Dear Anita and Vijay, thank you for considering our views on direct access. Representative Deshpande is welcome to propose an amendment on this topic next week. The following draft language is adapted from language we previously sought to introduce at the state level. Unfortunately, the recent State Electricity Act passed in March prohibits direct access and competition among electricity suppliers. Without a free electricity market and with all electricity purchases mandated through a state-controlled exchange, the taxpayers of Maharashtra bear the financial burden:

DRAFT LANGUAGE FOR DIRECT ACCESS IMPLEMENTATION
Within thirty days of enactment, the Independent Transmission Operator ("ITO") shall submit to the Central Energy Regulatory Commission ("CERC") a transmission congestion relief plan that includes physical rights to firm transmission across congestible interfaces. Such rights will grant users access to transmission without congestion charges. These rights will be valid for periods suitable to direct access market participants, up to one year, initially allocated via an annual auction supervised by the ITO and will be transferable.

Within thirty days of enactment, the program will enable direct access for large non-residential electricity consumers. It will require large industrial, commercial, and other non-residential users to meet their power needs by contracting with non-utility sources according to the following timetable:
- 90 days post-enactment: loads of 1 MW and above
- 180 days post-enactment: loads of 300 kW and above
- 270 days post-enactment: loads of 100 kW and above
- 360 days post-enactment: loads of 70 kW and above

This scheme allows large industrial, commercial, and other non-residential consumers to voluntarily contract for any portion of their electricity requirements with non-utility providers.

body:
Rajiv Menon will review the current status of this amendment in relation to the Sharma bill. However, we want to share our initial strong concerns regarding this amendment. We are quite worried that pursuing this amendment at the national level could jeopardize our efforts for energy savings initiatives and may lead to significant opposition against direct access itself. We plan to conduct some discreet consultations. At this stage, we believe this approach carries substantial risks. We are also reaching out to the Mumbai Commodity Exchange to understand their perspective.

Subject: Proposed Response - Summary of the Southern Power Deal
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Please find below some initial thoughts on our potential message.

It remains unclear how this arrangement will increase supply, reduce demand, or expand customer options. It still does not make sense to us that the government should acquire a deteriorating transmission network instead of funding essential public services.

We lack sufficient details. Several elements are intriguing and warrant further examination. The Chief Minister should release the specifics promptly so stakeholders can fully grasp the implications. For example, what will become of the Power Procurement Agency contracts? Will they be transferred to Southern Power? Will customers retain the right to choose in the future?

Recent developments underscore the urgent need to ensure customers can independently decide their energy sources going forward. We recognize that the government struggles to manage this correctly. The solution is to offer customers more choices, not fewer.

We cannot endorse this until we are certain our invoices will be paid in full. If payments are incomplete, a forced insolvency is highly probable.

Regrettably, this deal was not finalized sooner. It could have saved significant costs and hardship.

Why must the transmission purchase be included in this agreement? It may never materialize. Simplify the process—address the undercollection through securitization and the Southern Power refund, and move forward.

Regards,
Rajesh Kumar

---------------------- Forwarded by Rajesh Kumar / Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd. on 04/09/2024 19:24 ---------------------------
From: Anil Mehta on 04/09/2024 19:00
Sent by: Anil Mehta
To: Arvind Sharma/Delhi/AgricultureIndia, Divya Rao/Mumbai/AgricultureIndia, Rajat Singh/Hyderabad/AgricultureIndia, Neha Joshi/Pune/AgricultureIndia, Vipul Desai/Ahmedabad/AgricultureIndia, Priya Nair/Chennai/AgricultureIndia, Suresh Iyer/Kolkata/AgricultureIndia, Manish Gupta/Jaipur/AgricultureIndia
cc:

Subject: Summary of the MOU

Outlined below are the principal terms of the Southern Power Memorandum of Understanding:

• Power Commitment – Southern Power will maintain its current generation facilities and other generation assets and dedicate them to supplying power on a regulated cost-of-service basis for 10 years.
• Power Dedication – Southern Energy will commit the full output of Sunrise (one of its non-regulated generation facilities) to the State at a fixed price for 10 years. Phase I of Sunrise is to be operational by August 15, 2024. If not operational by this date, Southern Energy will incur a penalty of INR 15 crore.
• Transmission Sale – Southern Power will sell its transmission assets to the State for approximately INR 20,000 crore (2.3 times the net book value), subject to adjustments. Of this, INR 11,000 crore gain on sale will be applied to reduce Southern Power’s net undercollected amount as of January 31, 2024. The State will also assume certain liabilities related to the transmission assets.
• Backup Transaction – If the transmission sale does not occur within two years due to factors beyond either party’s control, the State may elect for Southern Power to sell its hydro generation assets. Should the hydro assets be valued below INR 11,000 crore, Southern Power will supply additional below-market-price power after December 31, 2034 to cover the shortfall.
• Conservation Easements – Southern Power will grant perpetual conservation easements to the State covering roughly 260,000 acres of its Big Creek hydroelectric lands and 825 acres of its Eastern Sierra hydro lands. Some land may be transferred in fee simple.
• Southern Energy Contribution – Southern Energy will refund Southern Power not less than INR 3,000 crore, including approximately INR 2,200 crore in estimated 2023 quarterly tax payments and INR 800 crore in federal loss carryback tax savings.
• Investment – Southern Energy and Southern Power will invest no less than INR 22,000 crore over the next five years in capital improvements.
• Litigation – Southern Power will dismiss specified claims, including takings and filed-rate doctrine cases.
• Regulatory Oversight – The State Energy Regulatory Commission will continue regulating Southern Power using established ratemaking principles.
• Payment for QF Drop-off – Southern Power will pay the net shortfall from January 18, 2024 to April 1, 2024 attributable to qualifying facilities not selling to Southern Power due to payment failures. This amount will be securitized.
• Securitization – Southern Power will securitize its full net undercollected amount (approximately INR 28,000 crore) in two tranches:
  - The first tranche will occur after legislation passage and signing definitive agreements, covering the net undercollection minus the gain on sale plus interest.
  - The second tranche will be triggered if the transmission sale does not occur within two years and will not appear in rates until then, if at all.
• Net Short Purchase – The State will cover the net shortfall through December 31, 2025. Afterward, Southern Power assumes responsibility.
• Investment Recovery – Southern Power will maintain an authorized rate of return no less than its current rate (11.6%) during the 10-year cost-of-service period.
• Next Steps (Definitive Agreements & Regulatory Actions):
  - Definitive Agreements – Following the MOU signing, parties will negotiate detailed agreements covering transmission sale, O&M, Transmission Services, and Facilities Services.
  - Regulatory Actions – Prior to definitive agreements, the State Energy Regulatory Commission will establish procurement cost preapproval mechanisms, defer Southern Power’s general rate case until 2026, grant some relief from direct access credits, and clarify holding company act priority conditions.

Date: Mon, 27 Oct 2025 06:50:23 -0400
From: Danielle Robinson <danielle.robinson@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
To: Brittany Gardner <brittany.gardner@lakeshoreutilities.gov>, Melissa Miller <melissa.miller@lakeshoreutilities.gov>, Reginald Gonzales <reginald.gonzales@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
Cc: Gwendolyn Glass <gwendolyn.glass@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
Subject: FW: GRI for Lakeshore Water
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

I'm not aware of any Lakeshore Water contracts that are structured this way, but it's been a while since I've reviewed contract rates. Do any of you recall situations where this may occur?

Thanks,
Megan

-----Original Message-----
From: Carter, Diane
Sent: Thursday, October 18, 2001 1:38 PM
To: Miller, Megan
Subject: GRI for Lakeshore Water

I believe that, back in 1998, Lakeshore Water changed the way they handled GRI to ensure that Reservation would not remit GRI if it was discounted. That would have increased Lakeshore Water's margin on certain contracts. However, the impact on margin would have declined by over 50% in 2001, when the Reservation GRI rate dropped from $0.0066/day to $0.0030. It will decrease again in 2002 when Reservation GRI becomes $0.0018.

Do you have any estimate of how many dollars Lakeshore Water will "lose" as a result of the decline in GRI?
On 1-part discounted rates, I would assume that there would be little impact. For example, if the market-driven rate is $0.10 then Lakeshore Water couldn't get more than $0.10 for the capacity, whether the max GRI surcharge were $0.0066 or $0.0018.

However, are there any long-term contracts where you collect GRI as part of the rate but do not remit it because of discounting?
For example, the discounted reservation rate is $0.20 plus GRI. Lakeshore Water billed $0.2066 in 2000 but $0.2030 in 2001 and $0.2018 in 2002.
As long as the total rate is below max, Lakeshore Water keeps the GRI piece, but the revenue on the contract drops each year as the GRI component goes down. (I don't know how many deals like this Lakeshore Water may have. Riverview Utilities has some.)

Subject: Key Achievements for the First Half of 2021
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

My key achievements for the first half of 2021 are as follows:

1. Developed New Trading Documentation – provided essential legal expertise and intellectual input to redesign trading forms to align more closely with standard industry templates.

2. Created Setoff and Netting Strategy during the Albion Power Group Insolvency – led the legal and credit teams across all Kestrel Aerospace divisions to minimise credit and legal exposure. This involved rapid assessment of the company’s positions and coordination across all units to determine the best approach to terminate and value Albion Power contracts.

Thank you, Rajesh. We will incorporate the additions you mentioned below. Bharat Agro (Suresh Kumar) will provide testimony on retail unbundling for the utilities. I agree that the mass-market retail stakeholders should also submit complementary testimony. Although we discussed this earlier, I have not yet received firm commitments from the retail participants to sponsor such testimony – this may be an oversight on my part. Nevertheless, retail testimony from market participants should include a discussion of benefits from GreenFields.com, AgroConnect, CUB, REMAC, and others. May I suggest that AgroCom Trading, as a major mass-marketer itself, coordinate this effort with the other retail partners?

Additionally, I urge all settlement parties to look beyond the testimony phase towards the hearings, scheduled to commence in just over a month. We will need to allocate time in late May for practice panels (assuming panel hearings are granted) and individual practice cross-examinations. At the same time, we should begin considering direct cross-examination of the SCGC/TURN parties (again, assuming we opt for full cross-examination of their settlement). There is value in cross-examining the opposing settlement as it appears inadequately developed, results in significant cost-shifts, and is inconsistent with the Commission’s most promising options. Conversely, there is merit in limiting our cross-examination, especially of Florio, who might use the witness stand to grandstand. Something for us to consider.

Subject: May 5 Testimony Preparation AGRI/COMMODITY SETTLEMENT

As you know, ALJ Biren has set May 5 as the deadline for testimony supporting all settlements filed on April 3 and April 17. While additional guidance may be provided at the PHC on April 24, we need to begin formalizing the testimony supporting the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement.

We have identified the content and responsible parties for drafting the testimony (listed below). The testimony will follow a "hub and spoke" format, where Bharat Agro will focus on the unbundling concepts, detailing how capacity and retail unbundling processes will operate. Other parties will file complementary testimony offering individual perspectives on why the settlement serves the public interest and benefits customers, India, and the agricultural community at large.

I propose the following deadlines for preparing and circulating testimony drafts so all signatories can review and provide input:

April 25 – Draft Outlines of Testimony (Optional)
April 28 – First Draft Testimony
May 2 – Second Draft Testimony
May 5 – File Testimony with Commission

It’s essential to circulate drafts twice to ensure everyone is clear on what will be filed on May 5. The schedule is tight but necessary within the given time constraints. The testimony assignments are as follows. There has been one update from our previous agreement: Bharat Agro will sponsor a witness on "Concepts of Unbundling." I also suggest filing all testimony as a single comprehensive document with a chapter-style format, though I’m open to suggestions.

Chapter 1 – Bharat Agro – Concepts of Unbundling
Chapter 2 – Bharat Agro – Mechanics of Unbundling: Capacity
Chapter 3 – Bharat Agro – Mechanics of Unbundling: Retail
Chapter 4 – ORA – Unbundling Policy and Core Impacts
Chapter 5 – WGS/WHP/AgroCom Trading – Transmission, Storage, and Balancing
Chapter 6 – Edison/CalAgri/Dynegy – Pricing and Benefits to Agricultural Commodity Generators
Chapter 7 – TXU/Shell – Core Interstate Capacity Unbundling
Chapter 8 – Transwestern – Primary and Secondary Receipt Point Access
Chapter 9 – Indicated Producers – Open Season and Impacts on Indian Production
Chapter 10 – CalAgri – Metering Program

Please share your thoughts.

Best regards,
Brian Cherry
Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd.
